The basics

What is an XML product feed?

A list of all products in a shop, saved as 1 file at a web address.

</>
XML

A text format for data. Each value sits between 2 labels: <g:price>28995.00 GBP</g:price>

?
Why it exists

A web standard since 1998, so systems can swap data without mistakes. XML has no fixed field names: Leadoo AI uses the Google Merchant Center standard (g:).

▦
CSV works too

A simple table: 1 row per product, 1 column per field.

<item>
  <g:id>CAR-3108</g:id>
  <g:title>2021 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid</g:title>
  <g:description>Automatic SUV, 27,600 mi, white</g:description>
  <g:link>https://dealer.example.com/rav4-3108</g:link>
  <g:image_link>https://dealer.example.com/rav4.jpg</g:image_link>
  <g:price>28995.00 GBP</g:price>
  <g:availability>in_stock</g:availability>
  <g:product_type>Used cars > SUV</g:product_type>
  <g:brand>Toyota</g:brand>
</item>

Start here Does the client run Google Shopping, Meta or TikTok ads with products? Then they already have a feed.

Ask the client for that feed URL and reuse it. A Google Merchant Center feed fits best. Check it is the full version, not one shortened for ads.

The client owns the feed: 100% responsible for the product data, its updates and a working link.

How it works

The whole thing in 4 steps

Step 1

The client gives the feed

A web address to an XML or CSV feed.

Step 2

Leadoo AI learns from it

The feed goes into a Product base and trains the AI. Refresh: every 24 hours by default, at most every 1 hour.

AI → Product base
Step 3

The bot searches it

Product Recommender, a block in the bot, looks for the closest products to what the visitor writes.

Bot Editor → Artificial Intelligence → Product Recommender
Step 4

The visitor sees products

Product cards with links. The closest one is marked Best match.

Node settings → Product Details
Strict search (a normal shop filter)
Hybrid automatic SUV under 20,000 GBP
0or very few results
= no sale

Every filter must match. 1 detail off: 0 or very few results, the visitor leaves, and there is no sale.

Product Recommender
Hybrid automatic SUV under 20,000 GBP
2019 Toyota C-HR Hybrid, automatic · 20,495 GBP
Everything fits except 495 GBP over budget
Best match
2018 Jeep Compass, automatic · 18,995 GBP
Petrol instead of hybrid
2021 Kia Niro Hybrid, automatic · 20,995 GBP
Hybrid SUV, 995 GBP over budget

Full and partial matches, sorted by relevance to the visitor's question. The visitor can refine: "cheaper", "only hybrid".

Shoppers often buy despite small compromises = sale

  • Questions first: any qualifying flow, no limit, in Give AI Instructions or with normal bot steps.
  • Full and partial matches: it shows both, sorted by default by relevance to the visitor's question.
  • Most relevant, not perfect: it can miss a better-matching product whose data uses other words.
  • Works well for: online shops and B2B catalogues, for example cars, furniture, packaging, fashion, electronics.
  • Not a good fit: travel, flights, prices that change many times an hour.

Product Recommender vs AI Chat

Almost the same engine,
different outcome

A Product base is a special kind of Knowledge Base, built from a feed. Problems and diagnosis are very similar.

AI Chat

Knowledge Base

A whole website, single URLs, or TXT, PDF and HTML files

Non-product questions: "Can I book a test drive?", "How long does delivery take?"

Product cards with image, name and link
A written answer
Weak answers

The 1 rule

The bot reads the Product base,
not the website

A detail that is only on the website does not exist for the bot.

1 source of truth
  • Feed data is never mixed with other sources.
  • So you always know where to look when results are weak.
  • Give AI Instructions don't add product data. They shape the conversation a lot, product selection only partially.
Why not read the website?

Scraping shop pages is unreliable:

  • Every shop is built differently. A redesign breaks the scraper.
  • Content loads late, so data goes missing without an error.
  • Shops block bots, for example with Cloudflare.
  • Prices and stock change, so data goes stale.

Even scraping vendors say so: Bright Data, PromptCloud, Ficstar.

Feed rules

What the feed must contain

You connect these fields in Map Your Data. Grey tag = Google Merchant Center name.

Must have Every product
  • Product ID g:id
  • Name g:title
  • Description g:description
  • Product URL g:link
  • Image URL g:image_link
  • Price g:price
  • Availability g:availability
Should have Much better results
  • Category g:product_type
  • Brand g:brand

The shop's own categories usually work better than g:google_product_category.

Nice to have If relevant
  • Discount price g:sale_price
  • Quantity g:quantity
  • Gender g:gender
  • Popularity g:popularity
  • Season g:season
Workaround

No field for it? The client adds it to Description

  • Only for details without their own field: colour, size, mileage, what it fits.
  • At the start of Description, as a labelled line.
  • Same labels, same order on every product.
  • Shoppers' words, including other names for the same thing.
  • 1 version per product, or the bot shows duplicates.
  • True, public facts only.

Visitors see this line on the card when you turn on Short Description.

<g:description>Year: 2021 | Mileage: 27,600 mi | Fuel: Plug-in Hybrid | Transmission: Automatic | Colour: White | Condition: Used
Family SUV, cheap to run for daily commuting.</g:description>

Setup and fix

The first version is a test,
not the final result

No bot reaches its target quality on the first try. Tell the client at the start. Use the same flow for a new bot and for fixing an existing one.

0 of 7 steps done0 of 0 checks
1

Upload the feed

3 min

Public URL (no login, VPN or bot blocker), XML or CSV, up to 250 MB and 25,000 products.

  • Loads, maps and imports without errors
AI → Product base → Create product base
2

Check the Product list

See what the AI knows, and whether it covers the client's use cases.

  • The data covers the client's use cases
  • The right feed fields are mapped
  • Image, price and availability are complete and match the website
AI → Product base → Edit → Product list
3

Check the node

  • The right Product base is selected
  • Give AI Instructions are clear and effective
Conversion Kit → Bot → Edit → Product Recommender
4

Test real-life questions

  • Ask like a real shopper: a need, a budget, a follow-up
  • Check which products come back
Bot Editor → Preview
5

Fix

  • Data wrong or missing: the client fixes the feed
  • Wrong field: you fix Map Your Data
  • Conversation wrong: you fix Give AI Instructions
6

Test again

  • Repeat steps 4 and 5 until results are good
  • Try different prompt setups to see what the prompt can and can't change
7

Still wrong? Report it

  • Bot link, Product base, questions, expected vs actual, screenshots
CS bugs: #leadoo-bugs-questions
CS feedback: #leadoo-product-suggestions
Sales, all: #leadoo-sales-product

Bring in the Product team for feeds over 25,000 products and 250 MB, feeds that can't be public, or results that stay wrong after this flow.

Pricing and FAQ

Questions CS and Sales get asked

Pricing

Paid monthly add-on, based on the number of products in the Product base.

ProductsGBP / monthEUR / month
Up to 2,000£99€99
2,000 to 5,000£149€149
5,000 to 10,000£199€199
10,000 to 15,000£249€249
15,000 to 25,000£299€299
  • Prices are for refresh every 24 hours. More frequent refresh, down to every 1 hour, may cost more.
  • A smaller feed can mean a lower tier.
  • Bigger catalogues: case by case. Always confirm with the current price list.
Setup
Which plans include it?

None by default. It is a paid add-on, sold as an upsell on top of the plan.

How is it switched on?

In the Leadoo Admin panel, once the add-on is sold.

Can we use more than 1 Product base?

Yes, up to 10 per account, set in the Leadoo Admin panel. Each Product Recommender uses 1 Product base, so build separate paths.

Can we put other data in an unused field, like location in Gender?

No, results become unpredictable. Workaround: Description.

Results
Can the price format be changed?

Not at the moment. It is fixed: 2 decimals, with the currency shown as text after the price, for example 28995.00 GBP.

We mapped Category. Why is it still wrong?

Words in Name and Description matter most. The phrase shoppers use, for example "hybrid SUV", must be in the right products.

Why products outside the category or budget?

It shows the closest products. Budget counts, but it is not a strict filter. Far above budget with correct prices: report it.

Why does "show more" show the same products?

Same question, same best matches. The shopper can ask for "different ones". You can try a rule like "do not repeat products" in Give AI Instructions, but it is not deterministic: sometimes it works, and when there are few other matching products it may not.

Why does it mention details that are not in the feed?

Add "use only Product base data" to Give AI Instructions. The client adds the missing details to the feed.

Expectations
Will a different AI model find better products?

Mostly no. The model changes how the bot talks, not which products it finds.

What quality can we promise?

No fixed percentage. Measure real results: recommendation CTR, or generated revenue if you have access to it.
